clue.text: Stars returned to reinvest

parts.note: the Plough is the group of seven stars also called the Big Dipper
something returned is given back

explanation.surface: Astrology talk: when the stars come back round, it is time to put money in again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it names one constellation, the Plough, which British solvers call the Big Dipper.
explanation.definitionFit: To put profits back into a business rather than paying them out is the verb phrase plough back.

clue.text: More stout or beer? That's about right

indicators.note: the word for beer goes about, surrounding the letter for right

parts.note: lager is a light beer

explanation.surface: A pub question: is stout or beer the right choice?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like the dark beer but is the adjective meaning fat; 'More stout' is bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stouter means being bigger or bulkier in size.

clue.text: Capsized upstart with prudent order

parts.note: the start of the word up is its first letter, U

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A boat flipped over by an arrogant newcomer who has prudent instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstart' looks like a brash newcomer but means the start of 'up', U, which joins PRUDENT in the anagram signalled by 'order'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that has overturned is upside down, bottom side facing up.

clue.text: Like a perpetual in-patient

parts.note: a patient who is always in rather than in hospital is someone who never leaves their home

explanation.definitionFit: Unable to leave one's home through illness or age, as if permanently confined indoors.

clue.text: Order alterations to two articles on weight

indicators.note: in a down clue the articles sit on top of the weight

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other form of the indefinite article
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Instructions to change a text by adding a couple of articles and a weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order alterations' means changes to the order of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another word's letters is a rearrangement of their sequence.

clue.text: Artist, in general, supporting king

indicators.note: in a down clue the general sits below, holding up the king

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: An artist who is generally a royalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'usually' but means inside the word for a general, LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter of the Bauhaus.

clue.text: It's. a term bandied about in abuse

indicators.note: words bandied about are tossed around, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: it's is spelled with the letters ITS

explanation.surface: A description of an insult being thrown around.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat badly or ill-use someone is to abuse them.

clue.text: Game in which sides are closely matched

definitions.text: Game in which sides are closely matched

parts.words: Game in which sides are closely matched
parts.note: closely means near in distance, not near in ability: a match between teams from the same area

explanation.definitionFit: A football or other match between two neighbouring teams from one town or district.

clue.text: Look round in the same place for, psychic energy

indicators.note: the word for look goes round, enclosing the abbreviation for the same place

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look! or behold
ibid., short for Latin ibidem, is the footnote abbreviation meaning in the same place

explanation.surface: Someone checking a footnote for a reference on mental force.
explanation.walkthrough: IBID is used in footnotes to say a source is the one just cited.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory the libido is the drive or mental force behind desire.

clue.text: Nymph transformed so trapped in locality

indicators.note: the word for so is held captive inside the word for locality

parts.note: an area is a locality or district
thus and so both mean in this way, therefore

explanation.surface: A mythical spirit, changed into something else, is caught in a district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' seems to be an anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: the nymph Arethusa was turned into a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Arethusa fled the river god Alpheus and was changed by Artemis into a fountain.

clue.text: Might it make teenager drunk? .Hardly

indicators.note: a drunk person is mixed up, so the letters of teenager are scrambled

explanation.surface: Asking whether a particular drink could get a youngster tipsy, and answering no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' signals the anagram and also hints the drink is drunk; the whole clue is the definition, since this mild drink is the last thing to intoxicate anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfermented Chinese or Japanese brew of unoxidised leaves contains no alcohol at all.

clue.text: Gun removing tail of goose

indicators.note: the final letter of the goose's name is cut off

parts.note: the brent is a small dark wild goose

explanation.surface: Instructions for shooting, cutting off a bird's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The BREN is the British light machine gun of World War II.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bren was a British light machine gun, a firearm named after Brno and Enfield.

clue.text: Novel: product with a short shelf-life

definitions.meaning: an item that sells so fast it barely stays on the shelf

explanation.surface: A book is described as goods that will soon go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short shelf-life' suggests something perishable; here it means something that sells out quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-selling book, and any goods that leave the shop shelves quickly because demand is high.

clue.text: Why say it's in Omaha or Utah when it's in Sussex?

indicators.note: the letter for why is placed inside the word for the D-Day landing sites

parts.note: Omaha and Utah were the American beachheads in the Normandy landings of 1944
say signals that the letter Y sounds like the word why

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why a place is in Normandy when it really lies on England's south coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Omaha and Utah look like US states, but they are the D-Day landing beaches. Sussex is a county on England's south coast; the answer is its famous chalk headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Beachy Head is the tall chalk cliff near Eastbourne on the English county's coast.

clue.text: Mother wit of one of Caligula's consuls?

definitions.meaning: native good sense or common sense
the emperor Caligula reportedly planned to make his horse Incitatus a consul, so this is that animal's judgement

explanation.surface: Asking about the native intelligence of a Roman official under a mad emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother wit is an old term for common sense, not anything to do with mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical common sense, and literally the wits of the steed Caligula wanted to make consul.

clue.text: Distance once used for sportsground.

definitions.meaning: the ancient Greek and Roman stade, about 185 metres, was a measure of length
an arena with tiered seats for watching games

explanation.surface: An old measure of length was applied to a place for games.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient running track took its name from its length, one stade.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the Greek stadion, a length of racecourse and then the arena built round it.

clue.text: Something out-of-date in this form of charisma

indicators.note: another form of the word gives the same letters in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A quaint trait in this kind of personal magnetism.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism is an outmoded word or usage, something old-fashioned.

clue.text: Rubbish' vehicle reversed into .another

indicators.note: the whole run of rubbish then vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: A refuse lorry backs into a second motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' applies to both words together, not just the vehicle. 'another' is the definition: another vehicle, picking up from 'vehicle' earlier in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine for pulling ploughs is a further type of vehicle beyond the cart.

clue.text: Spade, perhaps, a parent in US needed for plant

parts.note: a spade is an example of a playing card
mom is the American word for mother

explanation.surface: Gardening: a spade and an American mother are needed to set a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spade' looks like a garden tool but is a card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is a ginger-family plant grown for its aromatic seeds used as a spice.

clue.text: Transport and travels figure in this poem

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
goes means travels

explanation.surface: Vehicles and journeys feature in a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Cargoes is John Masefield's poem about three ships ('Quinquireme of Nineveh').
explanation.definitionFit: Masefield's well-known verse lists the freight of three ships through history.

clue.text: Officer.. acquired through .triumph .of hope over experience?

definitions.meaning: the merchant navy rank below the first mate
Samuel Johnson called a second marriage the triumph of hope over experience, so this is a partner got by marrying again

explanation.surface: A rank earned by optimism winning out over hard lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Dr Johnson's quip about remarriage, so the second sense is a spouse taken the second time round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's deck officer ranking next below the chief officer, and literally a spouse from a later marriage.

clue.text: Slightly blue fish caught therein

indicators.note: the letter for caught is placed inside the word for fish

parts.note: a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A fish, a bit sad-looking, has been landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour or mood but means risque; 'Slightly blue' is a joke that is a little rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Risque humour that is mildly indecent is called racy, as blue means smutty.

clue.text: Rebound part of chapter, we hear

indicators.note: the word for a member of the chapter is said aloud

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman who is a member of a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A section of a book chapter bounces back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chapter' looks like a book section but is a cathedral's governing body of clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cannon is to strike and bounce off something, as a billiard ball off another.

clue.text: Tending to take in reading, writing or arithmetic?

definitions.text: Tending to take in reading, writing or arithmetic?

indicators.note: the word for tending absorbs the letter standing for the school subjects

parts.note: leaning is inclining or tending towards something
these are the three Rs, so any one of them is an R

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to absorb the basic school subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic. The whole clue also describes study of those subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquiring knowledge through study, such as the basic school subjects.

clue.text: Article in Irish Times excels most leaders

indicators.note: the leading letters of the four words are taken in order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece in an Irish paper beats most editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' suggests newspaper editorials, apt with Irish Times, but means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A single newspaper piece or entry is an item.

clue.text: Appoint men to extract healing substance

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out from inside the run of words appoint men to

explanation.surface: Hire staff to draw out a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve rubbed on the skin to soothe or cure is a medicinal preparation.

clue.text: Four different courses for an ascetic

parts.note: east is one compass direction or course
south is a second compass course
south-east is a third compass course
north-east is a fourth compass course

explanation.surface: Choosing between four menu options for someone who denies themself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests a meal, but it means compass bearings: E, S, SE and NE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were a Jewish sect of the Second Temple era living a strict, self-denying communal life.

clue.text: Instructor has to look after genius

parts.note: a schoolmaster is an instructor or teacher
to mind is to look after

explanation.surface: A teacher must take care of a gifted child.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant person who plans a scheme is a mastermind, a synonym for genius.
